title: Extension of a coherent equivariant submodule across an invariant open
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be an affine group scheme of finite type over $F$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with action $a:G\times_FY\to Y$. A $G$-linearized quasi-coherent module means a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] $M$ with an isomorphism $a^*M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*M$ [def-pc-module-pullback] satisfying the identity and cocycle conditions; morphisms commute with these isomorphisms. A coherent linearized module is one whose underlying module is coherent. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ be an invariant open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], meaning $a^{-1}(U)=G\times_FU$ as open subschemes of $G\times_FY$. For every $G$-linearized quasi-coherent module $M$ on $Y$ and every coherent $G$-linearized submodule $N\subseteq j^*M$, there is a coherent $G$-linearized submodule $L\subseteq M$ whose restriction $j^*L\subseteq j^*M$ equals $N$ as a submodule with its given linearization. No coherence assumption is imposed on $M$ and no smoothness or reductivity assumption on $G$.

source.place: Agent-formulated consequence of Tag 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent) and Tag 09VH (lemma-pushforward), with Tag 077S (lemma-abelian). Coherence of images uses coherent.tex Tag 01Y1 (lemma-coherent-Noetherian-quasi-coherent-sub-quotient). These tags supply ingredients, not this exact extension statement.

proof.text: First verify the geometric hypotheses of the groupoid results. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is Noetherian: a field has only the ideals $0,F$, and its spectrum is one point. Hence $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Put $R=G\times_FY$ and $p=\operatorname{pr}_2$. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $p$ and $R\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ are of finite type, so the same Noetherian theorem makes $R$ Noetherian. The map $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field]; its base change $p$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. It is affine, quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], since $G$ is affine. The scheme isomorphism $\tau(g,y)=(g,gy)$ has inverse $(g,z)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}z)$ and satisfies $a=p\circ\tau$. Consequently $a$ has the same flatness, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness properties as $p$. These are identities of scheme morphisms furnished by the group action, and hold for nonreduced $G$ as well.

source.place: Tag 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent), hypotheses; supporting morphisms.tex Tags 01T3, 01T4, 01T6, 01U9, 01SD and 01S7

proof.text: Use the action groupoid with objects $Y$, arrows $R$, source $s=p$, target $t=a$, identity $e(y)=(1,y)$, inversion $(g,y)\mapsto(g^{-1},gy)$, and composition $((g,hy),(h,y))\mapsto(gh,y)$. The group and action identities verify exactly the laws of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]: sources and targets, units, inverses and associativity. With this convention the groupoid isomorphism $t^*M\to s^*M$ is precisely the given linearization $a^*M\to p^*M$; its two identities and the definition of equivariant morphisms agree with [def-sfb-scheme-groupoid-module]. Make the same identification on the invariant open $U$. Thus the groupoid results below apply to the given linearized modules, with no change of coefficient category.

source.place: Tag 03LI (definition-groupoid-module), specialized to the action groupoid

proof.text: The inclusion $j$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc]. It is quasi-separated because its diagonal is the identity after the canonical identification $U\times_YU=U$. Since $Y$ is quasi-compact, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2) makes $U$ quasi-compact; choose a finite affine open cover $(V_b)$ of $U$. Invariance gives both Cartesian squares for the groupoid map $(U,G\times_FU)\to(Y,G\times_FY)$: the source square is the product square, and the target square is the equality $a^{-1}(U)=G\times_FU$ in the hypothesis. The restricted groupoid on $U$ also has flat source and target, as needed for its abelian structure in step 4: its source $\operatorname{pr}_2:G\times_FU\to U$ is the base change of the flat map $G\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ [lem-pc-flat-field], and its target $a|_{G\times_FU}$ is the base change of the flat map $a$ along $j$ by the target Cartesian square, so both are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-cartesian-groupoid-pushforward-adjunction]. Ordinary $j_*$ therefore carries quasi-coherent linearized modules on $U$ to such modules on $Y$, and ordinary adjunction transposes of equivariant maps are equivariant. The underlying restriction $j^*j_*T\to T$ is the identity on every open contained in $U$, so its adjunction counit is an equivariant isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09VH (lemma-pushforward); properties.tex Tag 01OX and schemes.tex quasi-compact composition

proof.text: In the equivariant quasi-coherent category on $U$, form $Q=(j^*M)/N$. It is quasi-coherent and has its quotient linearization by [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-limits-colimits]. Transpose the quotient map $j^*M\to Q$ under the adjunction of step 3 to obtain an equivariant map $v:M\to j_*Q$. Define $P=\ker(v)$, with its inclusion into $M$. The same structural theorem computes this kernel on underlying modules and equips it with its induced linearization. Restricting this kernel to $U$ is sectionwise restriction of a kernel. Under the counit $j^*j_*Q=Q$, the restriction of $v$ is exactly the quotient map by the adjunction identity. Hence $j^*P=N$ as submodules of $j^*M$. This identification is equivariant: both are the kernel of the same equivariant quotient map, with its induced kernel structure. We have not asserted coherence of $P$.

source.place: Tags 077S (lemma-abelian) and 09VH (lemma-pushforward); kernel construction of the equivariant preimage

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-flat-noetherian-groupoid-coherent-approximation] to $P$ on the action groupoid: all its geometric hypotheses were verified in step 1. Obtain a small nonempty filtered diagram of coherent linearized modules $P_i$ with equivariant cocone $u_i:P_i\to P$. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-limits-colimits] this is a colimit of underlying module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-colimit-evaluation], on each affine $V_b\subseteq U\subseteq Y$ the cocone $P_i(V_b)\to P(V_b)=N(V_b)$ is a colimit of $\mathcal O_Y(V_b)$-modules. The $P_i$ need not be submodules of $P$.

source.place: Tags 07TU (lemma-colimit-coherent) and 077R (lemma-colimits), followed by affine evaluation

proof.text: For each affine $V_b$ of the finite cover, apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-affine-generators] with ambient scheme $U$, $H=N$ and $K=V=V_b$. It is compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and $N$ is coherent, hence of finite type. Obtain finitely many sections $n_{b,r}\in N(V_b)$ whose associated map from a finite free module sheaf surjects onto $N|_{V_b}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise](1), each $n_{b,r}$ lifts to a section of some $P_i(V_b)$. There are finitely many such sections over all $b,r$. Filteredness supplies a single object $i_0$ receiving arrows from their finitely many objects; transport each chosen lift along its arrow. The cocone identities say its image remains $n_{b,r}$. Thus $u_{i_0}|_{V_b}:P_{i_0}|_{V_b}\to N|_{V_b}$ is surjective as a sheaf map: its image contains the specified generators. This holds on every member of the cover, so $j^*u_{i_0}:j^*P_{i_0}\to N$ is surjective. If the list of generators is empty, use any object of the nonempty index category; if $U$ is empty, the same argument has an empty cover.

source.place: Tag 07TU applied with the finite-generator argument of properties.tex Tags 01PB (lemma-finite-type-module), 01PF (lemma-extend); algebra.tex Tag 00D6

proof.text: Let $L$ be the image of the equivariant composite $P_{i_0}\to P\hookrightarrow M$. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-limits-colimits], kernels and cokernels are computed on the underlying modules, so this image is a quasi-coherent linearized submodule of $M$ and is the quotient $P_{i_0}/\ker(P_{i_0}\to M)$. Its kernel is quasi-coherent. Since $Y$ is locally Noetherian and $P_{i_0}$ is coherent, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](2) makes this quotient coherent. Notice that the quotient theorem is applied to the coherent source $P_{i_0}$, not to the possibly noncoherent target $M$.

source.place: Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), image as kernel/cokernel; coherent.tex Tag 01Y1 (lemma-coherent-Noetherian-quasi-coherent-sub-quotient)

proof.text: Restriction to an open computes kernels and sheaf cokernels locally, hence computes images. The image of $j^*P_{i_0}\to j^*M$ is therefore $j^*L$. The map factors through $j^*P=N$ from step 4 and surjects onto $N$ by step 6, so this image is exactly the prescribed submodule $N$. All these maps are equivariant. The induced map $j^*L\to N$ is an isomorphism of underlying modules and therefore an equivariant isomorphism by the reflection assertion of [lem-sfb-groupoid-module-limits-colimits]. It commutes with the inclusions into $j^*M$, so the equality is of the specified submodules with their given linearizations. This is the required coherent linearized $L\subseteq M$.

source.place: Tag 077S (lemma-abelian), local computation of kernels and cokernels on the invariant open
